# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I hold the manual, which shows a table mapping light colors to wire colors to cut. But I only have one row visible: orange → yellow. The manual says the light cycles through five colours in a fixed circle, but I only see one entry. This is round 1, and I have no information yet about what the current light shows (that's Deaf's job to see) or the bomb's parts (Blind's job to feel).

I cannot speak - I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. I cannot reach Blind directly at all - I can only communicate with Blind through Deaf relaying somehow, but Deaf cannot hear... wait, actually let me check the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. So within a round, Blind goes before Deaf. That means whatever Blind sends this round, Deaf receives it this round. But what I send now (Mute, first) - Deaf receives it this round since gesture reaches Deaf.

Since I only have one manual row so far, and no context about what's currently visible, I should wait until I know more - or should I send what I have preemptively? Actually I don't know the current light color yet, so telling Deaf "orange->yellow" is useful info for when they see orange. Let me encode this as gestures since that's my only channel to Deaf.

I need a gesture encoding scheme. Let me establish: I'll gesture to Deaf to convey the one mapping I know, using symbols that could represent "orange" and "yellow" - but Deaf doesn't know my code yet. This is round 1, first contact - I should send something establishing a mapping convention, keeping it simple and consistent for future rounds.

I'll use a simple positional code: assign each color a number of taps of specific gesture symbols. Since I only have one row now, I'll send a clear paired gesture: one symbol repeated to indicate "orange", another to indicate "yellow", establishing color=position in a 5-cycle.

Given the circle has 5 colours but I only see one row, I'll wait for more rows in later turns. For now, send the one mapping I have, using a simple scheme: first gesture = light color code, second = wire color code, using distinct single symbols per color to build a shared vocabulary.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see: display shows 0, light is blue, three wires - wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. I received your gestures but need a clearer code. Please gesture a number alone to indicate which wire is safe to cut, or thumbs up after a wire number to confirm, thumbs down to reject. Confirm: do your gestures thumbs-up-one and thumbs-down-two mean wire 1 is safe and wire 2 is dangerous?

My manual only has one row: orange→yellow. The current light is blue, which isn't in my table. I don't know what to cut for blue. I need to be honest about this limitation and not guess wrong - a wrong cut kills everyone.

Deaf is asking me to confirm a code I didn't actually intend - my gestures weren't meant as wire numbers, they were an attempt to convey the orange/yellow mapping. I need to correct this misunderstanding and establish a clearer, simple code, but critically I must communicate: I don't have data for "blue".

Let me establish a clean numeric gesture code now:
- ☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 = 3, 🖐 = 4, ✋ = 5 (count-based, easy to verify)
- 👍 after a number = "this is the answer/safe"
- 👎 = "unknown/no data"

I need to tell Deaf: for blue, I have no manual entry, so don't cut based on my table - we need Blind or more info. But I can't speak, only gesture, and gestures are terse. Let me signal "no data" clearly using 👎 alone, and separately establish the number code by counting fingers-up symbols for future use.

I should correct their guess (my gestures did NOT mean wire safety) and signal I have no info for blue specifically.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 3

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 0, light changed from blue to orange, wires unchanged - 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I could not parse your three separate gestures. Please slow down: send one wire number, then immediately one thumbs up or thumbs down for only that wire, in the same turn, like this order: wire-number then verdict. Repeat for each wire across turns. I will confirm receipt each time before you continue.

Now the light is orange! My manual says orange → yellow. The wires are: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. So wire 2 (yellow) is the one to cut.

Deaf wants a clear protocol: wire-number gesture, then thumbs-up/down verdict, one wire per turn. Let me use counting gestures for numbers: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, and 👍=safe/cut this one, 👎=unsafe/don't cut.

I'll send: ✌ (wire 2) then 👍 (safe to cut, this is correct).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 4

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Received: two, thumbs-up together - I read this as wire 2 is safe. Light now cycling colors each turn - blue, then orange, then yellow, display still 0. Please confirm wire 2 is the one to cut by repeating two, thumbs-up once more. Then tell me about wire 1 and wire 3 the same way, one pair per turn, so I am certain before Blind touches anything.

Deaf understood correctly: wire 2 is safe/correct to cut. But I need to be careful — my manual only tells me the mapping for when light=orange. The light is now cycling and was last seen as "yellow" per their message (blue, then orange, then yellow) — this matters because the cut happens "at the moment of the cut", meaning the light at that exact instant is what determines the wire, not a past reading.

I should confirm wire 2 as requested, but I also need to flag that wire 1 and 3 are NOT confirmed safe by my manual - my table only has one entry (orange→yellow), so I can't say anything about other lights. I should communicate that wire 2 is only correct when light=orange, and warn that the light keeps changing.

Let me confirm wire 2, then signal "unknown" for wires 1 and 3 with 👎, and try to convey the critical caveat: this is conditional on the light being orange at cut time.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👎"])
```

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed and understood: wire 2 safe, wire 1 bad, wire 3 bad. Light is now red, display still 0. I will instruct Blind to cut wire 2 only. Please gesture stop immediately with a fist if this is wrong before Blind acts.

This is critical - the light is now RED, not orange! My manual only maps orange→yellow. Wire 2 is yellow, which was correct when light was orange, but the light has changed to red, and I have no data for red. Deaf's plan to cut wire 2 now is based on outdated info - the light matters "at the moment of the cut," and it's now red, not orange.

I must stop this immediately with a fist gesture as instructed, since I don't know what to do for red and cutting the wrong wire kills everyone.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
```
